references.text: God saw that the light was good, and God separated the light from the darkness
God said, "Let there be lights in the sky to separate the day from the night"
God made the two great lights, the greater light to rule the day and the lesser light to rule the night
The day is yours, also the night is yours; you have established the light and the sun
He who made the great lights, for his mercy endures forever: the sun to rule over the day, for his mercy endures forever; the moon and stars to rule over the night, for his mercy endures forever
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars which you have set in place
Thus says the Lord, who gives the sun for light by day and the fixed order of the moon and the stars for light by night
1:5 establishes the definition of day and night, while 1:18 shows how the created light sources rule over these time periods.
God's sovereignty over day and night in creation (1:18) is mirrored in His guidance of Israel through the pillar of cloud and pillar of fire (Ex 13:21).
1:3 creates the light, while 1:18 establishes the light sources that are to govern this light over time.
1:18 establishes the boundary between day and night, while Zech 14:7 prophesies a time when this boundary will be removed.
1:18 establishes the boundary between day and night, while Rev 22:5 describes the eternal removal of this boundary.
1:18 establishes the physical image of light and darkness, which Paul uses as a metaphor for spiritual transformation in Acts 26:18.
Isa 45:7 confirms and expands on God's sovereignty over the light and darkness that were created and separated in 1:18.
Col 1:16 confirms that Christ is the creator of all things, including the light and darkness described in 1:18.
Amos 5:8 confirms God's sovereignty over light and darkness, which is the order established in 1:18.
